title: Capacity waveform resonance causing transient kernel misselection — damping and microbatch admission controls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A recent capacity event in region us-west-2 produced repeated short-duration surges that triggered the scheduler's speculative probing logic. The probe sequence resonated with existing microbatch admission signals and led to transient 'waveform' amplification: many workers simultaneously switched to lower-latency but less-accurate kernels, causing a P95 latency spike and a small increase in model quality regression for a subset of customers.

Observed impact:
- P95 token latency increased from 120ms to 280ms for 3x bursts lasting 10–40s.
- Kernel-misselection rate (kernel chosen != expected for profile) rose from ~0.3% to 3.8% during spikes.
- KV-cache warmup inefficiency for affected requests produced extra GPU kernels executed per token.
- No data exfiltration or security impact. Customers with tight latency SLOs experienced degraded user-perceived responsiveness.

Hypothesis: 
A combination of (1) rapid autoscale/slot churn, (2) aggressive speculative probe rate, and (3) the current microbatch admission controller's instantaneous fill heuristic created a feedback loop where transient load oscillations amplified scheduler decisions. The scheduler's kernel scoring responded too quickly to short signals, so many agents simultaneously migrated to different execution paths.

Mitigation and action plan (short term):
1) Deploy configuration change: add a 5s exponential backoff window for speculative probes and reduce probe burst allowance by 60%. (Canary to 10% of runtime hosts.)
2) Implement admission-controller hysteresis: require microbatch fill ratio change to persist for 2 control intervals before admitting a different kernel family.
3) Emergency runtime knob: enforce a temporary conservative kernel override for customers with latency SLA flag set to true.

Implementation plan (medium term):
- Kernel score smoothing: add EWMA smoothing to per-worker kernel score with tunable tau; initial tau=8s.
- Admission policy: implement leaky-bucket admission gate so short-lived bursts do not flip microbatch configuration.
- Metrics and telemetry: add kernel-flip rate, admission-gate-failures, probe-amplification-index to the console dashboards and alerting rules.
- Canary strategy: rollout to 5% -> 25% -> 100% of hosts over 48 hours with automated rollback on kernel-flip-rate > 1% over baseline.

Testing and verification:
- Synthetic load test: replay the captured traffic trace (trace id: trace-capwave-2026-02-21) on staging with controlled burst patterns to verify smoothing and admission gates prevent resonance without harming steady-state throughput.
- Regression tests: add unit tests for EWMA math and admission-gate edge cases; integration test with scheduler and autoscaler mocks.

Runbook / Console updates:
- Add a new incident runbook section "capacity-waveform" including detection heuristics (kernel-flip-rate > 1% for > 15s + P95 increase > 80ms) and immediate steps (enable conservative kernel override, reduce probe_rate config).
- Dashboard: runtime-1.20 -> add per-host kernel histogram and probe-rate heatmap.

Owners and timeline:
- Owner (implementation): Miguel Torres (runtime team).
- Owner (observability + alerts): Priya Rao (SRE).
- Target for short-term config change: 2026-03-05 (applied to canary).
- Target for medium-term code rollout and full canary: 2026-03-24 (runtime-1.20).

Trade-offs considered:
- Increasing probe backoff reduces our ability to discover faster kernels during a legitimate long tail workload; mitigated by making the backoff configurable per-customer tier.
- EWMA smoothing introduces lag in adapting to real sustained workload shifts; we use canary and per-customer override flags to reduce customer risk.

Links to artifacts and PRs:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Capacity+Waveform+Damping+Design
- Staging replay trace: gs://redwood-staging/traces/trace-capwave-2026-02-21.jsonl
- Canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3821
- Observability dashboard draft: https://console.redwood.ai/d/waveform/Kernel+Waveform+Dashboard

Acceptance criteria (done):
- Kernel-flip-rate reduced to <=0.6% during synthetic burst tests that previously reproduced the issue.
- P95 under the same synthetic bursts reduced to within 20% of baseline.
- New dashboard panels and alerts created and acknowledged by SRE.

Notes:
- This ticket captures the follow-up actions after the ENG-299137 retro and coordinates with ongoing scheduler hardening work in ENG-421007 and canary guardrails in ENG-571203.
